newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-CONQUERORS VALENCIA FACE TRICKY TRIP TO PRAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CONQUERORS VALENCIA FACE TRICKY TRIP TO PRAGUE.

text.p: Valencia, who knocked holders Bayern Munich out of the UEFA Cup on Tuesday were rewarded with a tricky tie against Slavia Prague when the draw for the second round of the tournament was made on Friday.
Slavia are the current Czech League champions who took part in the preliminary round of the European Cup this season where they were eliminated by Grasshopper of Zurich.
Under new rules, clubs eliminated in the preliminary round of Europe's premier club competition now switch to the UEFA Cup for a second bite of the financial rewards on offer.
Slavia bounced back to beat Malmo of Sweden 5-2 on aggregate in the first round of the UEFA Cup.
Valencia, who thrashed Bayern 3-0 at home before losing the return leg 1-0, should advance and keep alive Spain's hopes of winning the UEFA Cup for the first time since Real Madrid won it in 1986.
Inter-Milan, who won the UEFA Cup in 1994 when they beat Casino Salzburg face Austrian opposition again when they meet Casino Graz.

English league club Newcastle who beat Hungarian opposition in the form of Ujpest Dozsa to win the old Inter Cities Fairs Cup, the precursor of the UEFA Cup, in 1969, return to Hungary to play Ferencvaros.
Ferencvaros are the current Hungarian champions and were also handed a UEFA Cup place after failing to win through to the Champions' League from the qualifying round after losing to Gothenburg.
Paris St Germain, the European Cup Winners Cup holders, continue the defence of their trophy against formidable Turkish opponents Galatasaray.
PSG breezed through the opening round 7-0 on aggregate against Liechtenstein part-timers FC Vaduz, but will have a far tougher battle against the Turks.

Liverpool, bidding to become only the fifth team to win all three of the European club competitions by winning the Cup Winners Cup this season, will be meeting a club who have won the Swiss League just once, in 1992.

Liverpool's chief executive Peter Robinson said: "The one thing we will not be doing is under-estimating the opposition. When we were drawn against Brondy last season many people thought we would win and we did not. Believe me, from experience we know not to under-estimate the opposition."
Sion's general manager Leon De Riedmatten was concerned about the influx of English fans to his stadium.
"We will be working very closely with both the English and our own police forces," he said.
"We will taking measures before and after the game to ensure there is no trouble and English officers will come to Switzerland next week to assess the situation."
Barcelona, one of the sides who have won all three European trophies, face Red Star Belgrade, who won the Champions Cup in 1991, a year before Barcelona won the title.
Barcelona spokesman Amador Bernabev said: "This is a very difficult match for us. We know it will be very hard in Yugoslavia, they have a big stadium and very passionate fans."
